title: Smooth and marked associated log charts over a log regular pair
statement: Let $Y$ and $W$ be locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $T\subseteq Y$ be closed, and suppose $(Y,T)$ is a log regular pair with divisorial log structure $M_Y$ [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. Suppose $M_Y$ has a chart $P\to M_Y$ by a fine saturated monoid, with structure map $\alpha:P\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Consider either of the following data: (i) a smooth morphism $g:W\to Y$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with $E=\varnothing$; or (ii) an etale $Y$-morphism $c:W\to\mathbf A^1_Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space], with $g$ its composite to $Y$, coordinate $z=c^*(t)$, and $E=V(z)$. Put $B=g^{-1}(T)\cup |E|$ and $U=W\setminus B$. In case (i) let $L$ be the log structure associated to $P\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$, $p\mapsto g^*\alpha(p)$; in case (ii) let $L$ be associated to $P\oplus\mathbf N\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$, $(p,n)\mapsto g^*\alpha(p)z^n$, using the associated log structure of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Then $L$ is fine saturated and the inclusion of the base chart defines a morphism $(W,L)\to(Y,M_Y)$. Its groupified chart map is injective, with cokernel $0$ in case (i) and $\mathbf Z$ in case (ii). The comparison with the monoid-algebra base change is respectively $g:W\to Y$ and $c:W\to\mathbf A^1_Y$. The log scheme $(W,L)$ is log regular, its triviality locus is exactly the dense open $U$, and its structure map canonically identifies $L$ with $\mathcal O_W\cap j_*\mathcal O_U^\times$, where $j:U\hookrightarrow W$. Consequently $B$ is nowhere dense and $(W,B)$ is a log regular pair.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9, printed pp. 70--71, smooth-locus case; VI 1.8 and 1.4: base chart P and marked chart P direct sum N, comparison, triviality locus and divisorial recovery.

proof.text: Put $Q=P$ in (i) and $Q=P\oplus\mathbf N$ in (ii), with $h=1_P$ or $h(p)=(p,0)$. The latter monoid is fs: finite generation and the embedding in $P^{\rm gp}\oplus\mathbf Z$ hold componentwise; if $n(a,b)\in P\oplus\mathbf N$ for $n>0$, saturation gives $a\in P$ and $b\geq0$. Thus the associated structure $L$ has an fs chart by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The chart maps satisfy $\beta(h(p))=g^*\alpha(p)$. On associated-log stalk pushouts, send the class of $(p,u)$ to the class of $(h(p),g^*u)$; a relation coming from a base chart element mapping to a unit is respected since its pullback is a unit. These maps commute with restriction and the structure maps, giving the required log morphism.

source.place: VI 1.1 and Proposition 1.9, smooth-locus assertion, pp.69--71; explicit associated-chart construction.

proof.text: The groupified map is respectively $1_{P^{\rm gp}}$ or $a\mapsto(a,0)$ into $P^{\rm gp}\oplus\mathbf Z$, hence injective with cokernel $0$ or $\mathbf Z$. In the monoid-ring convention of [lem-trf-log-smooth-log-regular], $\mathbf Z[P\oplus\mathbf N]=\mathbf Z[P][t]$: the basis element $[p,n]$ maps to $[p]t^n$, with inverse on the same basis. Therefore the comparison target is $Y$ in (i) and $\mathbf A^1_Y$ in (ii), by [def-sbc-affine-space]. Affine locally this is $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[P][t]\simeq A[t]$, sending $a\otimes[p]t^n$ to $a\alpha(p)t^n$, with inverse $at^n\mapsto a\otimes t^n$. The comparison map pulls $t$ back to $z$, so it is precisely $c$ in (ii), and is $g$ in (i). These identifications agree on restrictions since they fix the base and the coordinate.

source.place: VI 1.8 and Proposition 1.9 chart test, pp.70--71; explicit monoid-ring base-change computation.

proof.text: At a geometric point $\bar w$ over $\bar y$, the map of strict local rings is local, so an element of $\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$ pulls back to a unit exactly when it is a unit (nonunits lie in the maximal ideal, whose image lies in the target maximal ideal). By the chart pushout of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], the associated log stalk is trivial exactly when all chart elements have unit image: if they do, the pushout is the unit group; conversely a log unit has unit structural image. In case (i) this is equivalent to $M_Y$ being trivial at $\bar y$, hence to $\bar y\notin T$ by [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. In case (ii) it additionally requires $z$ to be a unit at $\bar w$, equivalently $\bar w\notin V(z)$. Thus the triviality locus of $L$ is exactly $U=W\setminus B$ in both cases.

source.place: VI 1.4 and Proposition 1.9, pp.69--71; associated-chart unit calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-log-smooth-log-regular] to the constructed log morphism. Both schemes are locally Noetherian by hypothesis, the charts are fs by step 1, the base is log regular by [def-trf-log-regular-pair], the group map has torsion-free cokernel by step 2, and its comparison is the stipulated smooth $g$ or etale $c$. The cited theorem gives log regularity of $(W,L)$, a dense open triviality locus, and the canonical structural identification with $\mathcal O_W\cap j_*\mathcal O_U^\times$. Step 3 identifies that locus with the specified $U$. Since $T$ and $V(z)$ are closed, $B$ is closed; density of $U$ means that $B$ is nowhere dense. With the same divisorial identification, the fs and log-regular conclusions say exactly that $(W,B)$ is a log regular pair [def-trf-log-regular-pair].

proof_origin.place: VI 1.1, 1.4, 1.8 and Proposition 1.9 (printed pp.69--71): expanded smooth-locus argument through existing chart criterion.
